numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Datetimelike arithmetic that produces a result exactly equal to the NaT sentinel (NPY_NAT / NPY_DATETIME_NAT, INT64_MIN) returns a missing value (NaT) instead of raising the same overflow/out-of-bounds error that occurs for the neighbouring one-step-further-out case.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: For scalar paths: raise OutOfBoundsDatetime when the computed int64 result equals NPY_NAT. For array/vectorized paths: raise OverflowError for the same sentinel-landing case (rather than returning NaT).
trigger_conditions: A datetimelike arithmetic operation where the computed int64 sum/difference lands exactly on the NaT sentinel NPY_NAT/NPY_DATETIME_NAT (INT64_MIN), making it indistinguishable from a missing value downstream
Scalar Timestamp + Timedelta (or Timestamp - Timedelta delegated into _Timestamp.__add__) where the result equals NPY_NAT (e.g., pd.Timestamp.min + pd.Timedelta(-1, "ns"))
Array arithmetic on DatetimeIndex/TimedeltaIndex/PeriodIndex where the result equals the NaT sentinel exactly (one step inside), e.g., adding/subtracting by 1 ns around the min boundary

(Code-level trigger) Shared array kernel add_overflowsafe computes res_value as NPY_DATETIME_NAT after lval/rval addition; it previously did not check for this case before writing the result, so it returned NaT instead of raising

oracle_clues: NPY_NAT is INT64_MIN; a result exactly equal to NPY_NAT would be indistinguishable from missing downstream, so it must be treated as overflow/out-of-bounds.

Scalar fix: in pandas/_libs/tslibs/timestamps.pyx, after new_value = self._value + nanos, if new_value == NPY_NAT it raises OutOfBoundsDatetime instead of returning a Timestamp value equal to the NaT sentinel.

Array/kernel fix: in pandas/_libs/tslibs/np_datetime.pyx, in add_overflowsafe, after computing res_value, if res_value == NPY_DATETIME_NAT it raises OverflowError instead of returning a value representing NaT.

numerical_characteristics.dtype: datetime64[ns] (also covers datetime64 with units s/ms/us/ns; and timedelta64[m8 units]; and period[D])
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: sum/difference one step inside int64 range that lands exactly on iNaT/NPY_DATETIME_NAT (INT64_MIN); neighbouring values one step further out are reported as out-of-bounds
category_specific_evidence: Fix: treat results that equal NPY_DATETIME_NAT (NaT sentinel) as overflow because i) int64 can hold the sum, but ii) the value is indistinguishable from a missing value downstream (GH#66549).
BUG description: results landing exactly on the NaT sentinel returned NaT (GH#66549); NPY_NAT is INT64_MIN, so a sum that lands exactly there is indistinguishable from missing downstream.

DatetimeIndex test: construct dti = DatetimeIndex(np.array([iNaT + 1], dtype=f"M8[{unit}]")); then obj + Timedelta(-1, unit) and obj - Timedelta(1, unit) should raise OverflowError with match 'Overflow in int64 addition'.

TimedeltaIndex test: construct tdi = TimedeltaIndex(np.array([iNaT + 1], dtype=f"m8[{unit}]")); then tdi - Timedelta(1, unit) and tdi + Timedelta(-1, unit) should raise OverflowError with match 'Overflow in int64 addition'.
Period test: pi = pd.PeriodIndex([pd.Period(ordinal=iNaT + 1, freq='D')]); then pi - 1 and pi + pd.offsets.Day(-1) should raise OverflowError with match 'Overflow in int64 addition'.
reproduction_risks: Requires using values where the arithmetic result exactly equals the NaT sentinel NPY_DATETIME_NAT/iNaT (INT64_MIN), i.e., landing on the missing-value representation rather than being merely out-of-bounds.
Must cover multiple time units: unit in ['s','ms','us','ns'] as used by the added array tests.
For datetime, array-based and tz-aware paths are both exercised by localizing to 'UTC' in the test.
